text:
### Observed differences

- The two windows show a clean handover between two activities. In the earlier window, A03 ran in about 45 in 100 traces (mean about 0.95 occurrences per trace, with repeats in about 25 in 100), while A01 was not observed at all; in the later window, A03 was not observed in any of the 200 traces, while A01 ran in about 50 in 100 traces (mean about 1.0 per trace, repeats in about 28 in 100). [OCC001, OCC002]
- A01 inherited A03's incoming links. Earlier, about 52 in 100 of A09's observed outgoing transitions led to A03, and about 22 in 100 of A11's did; in the later window these lead to A01 instead (about 55 in 100 from A09, about 18 in 100 from A11), and transitions into A03 are gone. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]
- The two activities have nearly identical outgoing profiles. Earlier, A03's outgoing transitions went about 45% to A11, 18% to A10, 18% to A09 and 14% to A12; in the later window, A01's go about 46% to A11, 16% to A12, and about 15% each to A09 and A10. [DIR001, DIR002]
- Both occupy a similar relative position in the trace: A03's median position was about 0.39 of the trace earlier, A01's is about 0.38 in the later window (event positions, not clock time). [POS001, POS002]
- Co-occurrence relations moved from A03 to A01. Earlier, A03 co-occurred with A09 and A11 in about 45 in 100 traces, with A05 in about 38, with A10 in about 33 and with A12 in about 28; in the later window A03 co-occurs with none of them, while A01 co-occurs with A09 and A11 in about 50 in 100 traces, with A05 in about 44, and with A10 and A12 in about 35. A01 and A03 never appear in the same trace in either window. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that A01 took over the point in the process where A03 used to run. In the earlier window, A09 and A11 led mainly to A03, A03 continued mainly to A11, A10, A09 and A12, and it co-occurred with A05, A09, A10, A11 and A12; in the later window the same links attach to A01 — A09 leads to A01 in about 55 in 100 of its transitions and A11 in about 18, A01's outgoing transitions go to A11, A12, A09 and A10 in nearly the same proportions, at a similar relative position and with similar participation and repetition levels — while A03 is no longer observed. A01 and A03 never occur in the same trace, consistent with one coded activity occupying the position the other held. The change is shown directly by the successor changes at A09 and A11 and the mirrored co-occurrence patterns, not only by the participation counts, and the number of qualifying items (19, against roughly 0.33 expected if nothing had changed) is far beyond what an unchanged process typically produces. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, POS001, POS002, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011]

A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that A01 and A03 are the same underlying step recorded under different anonymous codes: their outgoing profiles and positions are nearly identical, so the evidence shows the change in coded behaviour but not what the codes refer to. The windows are also finite samples of 200 traces each, so small differences within the successor mix could partly be sampling variation. [DIR001, DIR002, POS001, POS002]

Other differences: beyond the A03-to-A01 handover, A11's remaining outgoing shares shifted slightly (A12 up from about 26% to 31%, A10 down from about 28% to 25%, A09 up from about 5% to 9%), and A05 itself appeared somewhat more often (about 64 in 100 traces earlier versus about 75 in the later window). [DIR004, REL002, REL007]
